canonical_statement: Provisional source-faithful family: for a stochastic process X on a measurable state space, the conditional law of its future after a deterministic time, given the past up to that time, depends on the past only through the present state. The repository does not specify a process construction or hypotheses from which this property is to be proved.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: a probability space Omega, a measurable state space E, a linearly ordered time domain T, an E-valued process X indexed by T, and a filtration representing its past; exact structures and Lean universes remain open.
quantifiers: filtration F to which X is adapted
measurable future events or bounded measurable test functions
hypotheses: measurability and adaptedness needed to form the conditional laws
regularity or standard-Borel assumptions needed by the chosen conditional-distribution encoding
any time-homogeneity, initial-law, transition-kernel, conservativity, or path assumptions required by the selected source theorem
conclusion: A selected conditional-law or conditional-expectation identity expressing that conditioning on the past at time s gives the same future prediction as conditioning on X_s alone.

alternate_encodings.target: conditional expectation of f(X_t) given F_s is a measurable function of X_s
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate equivalent formulation under additional measurability hypotheses

alternate_encodings.target: regular conditional law of X_t given F_s equals a transition kernel evaluated at X_s
future path is conditionally independent of the past given X_s
strong Markov property at stopping times
alternate_encodings.relationship: strictly stronger neighboring claim unless separately derived

excluded_degenerate_cases: Not yet frozen. At minimum s = t, trivial filtrations, deterministic processes, null-set versions of conditional laws, empty/degenerate state spaces, killed or explosive processes, and non-time-homogeneous processes require explicit treatment.
